early.gujarati: pCod uporthI pILo thava maMDe, nIchethI sukI jay
early.hindi: ऊपर से पीला होना शुरू, नीचे से सूखना
early.english: Yellowing of leaves starting from top, vascular discoloration

late.gujarati: puro CoDa sukI jay, nI vaeLI suki Jay, mulma kalo rang
late.hindi: पूरा पौधा सूख जाता है, जड़ें काली हो जाती हैं
late.english: Complete wilting and death of plant, brown to black root discoloration, stem shows vascular browning

favorable_conditions.soil: Heavy soil with poor drainage, light soil with poor water retention
favorable_conditions.weather: Hot weather after waterlogging OR prolonged drought

causes: Poor soil drainage leading to waterlogging
Light soil lacking water retention causing drought stress

cultural: Ensure proper field drainage before sowing
Improve soil water retention with organic matter
Deep summer plowing to reduce soil-borne fungi
biological: Apply Trichoderma viride/harzianum in soil at sowing
Use well-decomposed FYM to improve soil microbiome

chemical_treatment.note: No effective chemical cure once wilting appears; prevention is key
chemical_treatment.soil_treatment: Carbendazim 50WP 2g/L water as soil drench around base of plant at early symptoms

organic_treatment: Cotton stalk compost with beneficial microorganisms
Soil drenching with Trichoderma-enriched FYM slurry
etl: N/A - remove and destroy infected plants immediately
government_recommendation: Use disease-resistant varieties; crop rotation (3 years minimum); improve soil drainage; apply Trichoderma at sowing
region_specific: More severe in waterlogged heavy black cotton soils of Saurashtra and North Gujarat
embedding_chunk: Cotton Fusarium Wilt (Sukaro) is a soil-borne fungal disease causing yellowing and wilting from top down. Caused by Fusarium oxysporum in heavy soils with poor drainage. Prevention: resistant varieties, proper drainage, Trichoderma application. No cure after wilting - remove infected plants.
name: Cotton Wilt / Fusarium Wilt

visual.gujarati: phUl gulabjevi Racha (rosette), DoDa khaRI paDe, DoDama chhidra
visual.hindi: गुलाब जैसे फूल (Rosette), टिंडे गिरना, टिंडे में छेद
visual.english: Rosette-shaped flowers (locked flowers), boll shedding, circular holes in bolls, pink larvae inside bolls

economic_threshold_level.measurement: 1 rosette flower per plant OR 1 damaged boll per 10 bolls inspected
economic_threshold_level.monitoring: Pheromone traps: if average catch exceeds 8-10 moths per trap per night over 3 consecutive nights

life_cycle.overwintering: Pupae overwinter in soil and crop residue

favorable_conditions: Late season (September-November); high humidity; continuous cotton cropping

monitoring.pheromone_traps: Install 5-10 traps per hectare for pink bollworm
monitoring.field_inspection: Check flowers and bolls weekly after flowering

cultural: Deep plowing in summer to destroy overwintering pupae
Destroy all crop residue after harvest
Plant trap crop Galgota/Castor 1 row per 10 rows of cotton
biological: Install pheromone traps (5-10/ha) for monitoring and mass trapping
NPV (Nuclear Polyhedrosis Virus) spray: 450 LE/ha, spray in evening every 10-15 days

government_recommendation: IPM first: pheromone traps + NPV spray; chemical only if ETL exceeded; plant trap crops; destroy crop residue; deep summer plowing
embedding_chunk: Pink Bollworm (Bhuri Iyad) in cotton - rosette-shaped flowers, boll shedding, pink larvae inside bolls. ETL: 1 rosette per plant. IPM: pheromone traps 5-10/ha, NPV 450 LE/ha evening spray. Chemical: Quinalphos 20ml/10L or Acephate 15g/10L only at ETL. Cultural: deep summer plow, destroy crop residue.
name: Pink Bollworm

visual.english: Circular holes bored into bolls, larvae visible at boll entry with frass (droppings), flower bud shedding, larvae feed on tender plant parts

etl: 2 larvae per 10 plants in vegetative stage; 1 larva per plant in flowering stage

biological: HaNPV (Helicoverpa NPV) spray: 250 LE/ha in evening every 10-15 days
organic: Neem oil 3% spray + neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) 5%
Hand-pick and destroy larvae and egg masses

government_recommendation: Use HaNPV first; intercrop with trap crops; chemical spray only at ETL
embedding_chunk: American Bollworm (Helicoverpa armigera) - circular holes in cotton bolls, frass at entry. ETL: 1 larva/plant at flowering. Spray HaNPV 250 LE/ha evening, or Quinalphos 20ml/10L water at ETL.
name: American Bollworm / Helicoverpa

leaf_blast.english: Diamond/spindle-shaped spots with gray center and brown border on leaves

neck_blast.english: Neck rot causing white empty panicles (white ear or deadheart at neck)

symptoms.severity: Neck blast is most damaging - entire panicle becomes empty

favorable_conditions: High humidity (>90%), temperature 20-28°C, excessive nitrogen fertilizer, susceptible varieties

management.seed_treatment: Soak seeds in Streptocycline 600g + Emisan-6 (Parachlorophenol) 12g in 24L water for 8-10 hours before planting
cultural: Reduce nitrogen fertilizer at blast-prone stages
Drain field temporarily to reduce humidity

government_recommendation: Seed treatment is mandatory; spray Tricyclazole or Carbendazim at 15-day intervals when symptoms appear; avoid excess nitrogen
embedding_chunk: Rice Blast (Jhad) - fungal disease by Pyricularia oryzae. Diamond-shaped spots on leaves; neck rot causing empty panicles. Seed treatment: Streptocycline 600g + Emisan-6 12g/24L water, 8-10 hours soak. Spray: Tricyclazole 6g/10L or Carbendazim 10g/10L every 15 days.
name: Rice Blast

visual.english: Silver shoots (silver-colored hollow tubes), onion-leaf shaped tillers - pipelike hollow structure instead of normal tiller

etl: 1 silver shoot per 10 tillers at early stage

cultural: Clip tips of seedling leaves before transplanting to destroy eggs

chemical.timing: 15 days after transplanting in gall midge-prone areas

government_recommendation: Carbofuran 3% granules 15 days after transplanting in endemic areas; clip seedling tips before transplanting
embedding_chunk: Gall Midge (Gambharo) in rice - silver shoots/onion leaf tillers. ETL: 1 silver shoot/10 tillers. Control: Carbofuran 3% granules 100g/10x10m area at 15 days after transplanting. Or spray Rhizophos 40EC 12ml/10L.
name: Gall Midge

visual.english: Oval to irregular water-soaked lesions on leaf sheaths, green-gray center with brown borders, lesions coalesce causing sheath rot and lodging

embedding_chunk: Rice Sheath Blight (Karatan) - Rhizoctonia solani causes oval lesions on sheaths. Spray Mancozeb 75WP 30g/10L water every 10 days.
name: Sheath Blight / Sheath Rot

visual.english: Yellow or orange-yellow powdery pustules in streaks or scattered on leaves and stems; premature leaf drying; yield loss
visual.gujarati: pAn ane dAMDI par nArangi-pILo/nArangi chUrNiya phoDa, pAn vhelA sukI jAy

favorable_conditions: Cool nights (10-15°C) + warm days; high humidity; susceptible varieties
prevalence: Saurashtra coastal belt, North Gujarat and Central Gujarat
etl: First appearance of symptoms - spray immediately

chemical_spray.timing: 3 sprays from symptom appearance, every 15 days
3 sprays from symptom appearance, every 15 days

cultural: Timely sowing (November 15-25) to avoid rust-favorable weather

government_recommendation: Plant resistant varieties; spray Zineb or Mancozeb 0.2% solution 3 times at 15-day intervals from first symptoms
embedding_chunk: Wheat Rust (Geru) - Puccinia species causes orange-yellow powdery pustules on leaves. Common in Saurashtra coastal and North/Central Gujarat. Spray Zineb 0.2% or Mancozeb 0.2%, 3 times at 15-day intervals from first symptom.
name: Wheat Rust (Yellow Rust / Brown Rust)

visual.english: Plants pulled out easily as roots are destroyed; yellowing and death of tillers; white tunnels in soil around plant base

prevalence: Most severe in North Gujarat in non-irrigated wheat

chemical.method: Mix in 5L water, mix with 100 kg sand, sprinkle in field when termites appear and irrigate

cultural: Seed treatment with Chlorpyrifos before sowing

embedding_chunk: Termites (Udhai) in wheat - roots and stems destroyed, plants easily pulled. Common in North Gujarat rainfed wheat. Control: Chlorpyrifos 20EC 450ml/ha mixed with 100kg sand, sprinkle when visible.
name: Termites in Wheat

visual.english: Sudden wilting even with moisture, yellowing of leaves, root and stem base shows dark brown discoloration, plant death within days

favorable_conditions: Waterlogged soil, high temperature, infected seed, continuous castor cropping

cultural: Plant resistant varieties GCH-4, GCH-6, GCH-7
Remove and destroy infected plants immediately
soil_treatment: Trichoderma harzianum 5kg mixed with 500kg castor shells, apply in furrows at sowing

government_recommendation: Crop rotation 3 years minimum; resistant varieties GCH-4,6,7; Trichoderma in soil; seed treatment with Thiram/Carbendazim
embedding_chunk: Castor Wilt (Sukaro) - Fusarium oxysporum causes sudden wilting, yellowing, plant death. Control: 3-year rotation, resistant GCH varieties, seed treat Thiram 3g/kg, Trichoderma harzianum 5kg+500kg castor shells in soil.
name: Castor Wilt / Fusarium Wilt

visual.english: Complete defoliation - larvae eat all leaves, characteristic looping movement of larvae, severe damage can kill young plants

cultural: Deep plowing after harvest to destroy pupae in soil

embedding_chunk: Castor Semilooper (Ghodiya Iyad - Achaea janata) - complete defoliation of castor. ETL: 4 larvae/plant. Chemical: Quinalphos 20ml/10L or DDVP 5ml/10L water. Severe: Quinalphos 1.5% dust 25kg/ha.
name: Castor Semilooper

disease_name.gujarati: VanIya ghI - cHal sagrahe JIvAt (Rice Weevil)

visual.english: Round holes in grains, hollow grains, grain dust in storage, grain stuck together
visual.gujarati: dANA polA thAy, dANA ma gol chHIdra, chhAN (wheat dust)

entry_route: Field infestation at grain maturity; already infested old storage containers
prevention: Clean and disinfect storage bins/bags before use
Store with neem leaves (2 kg per 100 kg grain)
Apply Malathion 0.1% on sacks before filling

chemical_treatment.dose: 1 tablet per 100 kg grain (3 tablets per tonne)
chemical_treatment.procedure: Place in airtight storage for 7 days; ventilate before opening
chemical_treatment.safety_caution: TOXIC - wear protective equipment; never inhale; phosphine gas is lethal

chemical_treatment.dose: 0.1% solution sprayed on sacks before filling

organic_treatment: Neem leaves (Limdo) 2 kg mixed with 100 kg grain - acts as natural repellent
Castor leaves (Divela) used as natural insect repellent in storage
Sun drying grain for 2-3 days before storage
government_recommendation: Dry grains properly; use Aluminium Phosphide fumigation for large storage; neem leaves for small storage
embedding_chunk: Rice Weevil in grain storage - hollow grains, circular holes. Prevention: dry to <10% moisture, clean storage bins, neem leaves 2kg/100kg grain. Treatment: Aluminium Phosphide 1 tablet/100kg, airtight 7 days. Malathion 0.1% on sacks.
name: Rice Weevil
namegu: VanIya ghI - cHal sagrahe JIvAt (Rice Weevil)
